We have run into trouble and hoped we might borrow your assistance.
These two girls are actually sisters.
Lately many minors fake their age using an older sister's ID for pocket money.
When someone brings a license this identical, even we cannot tell them apart.
If you could simply tuck this envelope into your pocket.
Let me treat the three of you to deluxe grilled eel boxes.
I don't want it! I hate eel anyway.

Hold on a second, what the heck is going on here!
All right, good work, gentlemen. Cancel the eel boxes.
Thanks for your trouble.

meanings.note: Polite/honorific form of 忙しい with prefix お.

examples.text: お忙しいところすみません。
examples.trans: Sorry to bother you while you're busy.

meanings.note: Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.
Everyday noun for time on the clock or a dedicated stretch of time.

examples.text: まだ少し時間があります。
examples.trans: There is still a little time.

examples.text: 楽しい時間をありがとう。
examples.trans: Thank you for the fun time.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

examples.text: 楽しみです。実はお伝えしたいことがあって。
examples.trans: I'm looking forward to it. Actually, there's something I wanted to tell you.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

困る.gloss: be troubled; be in a bind

meanings.en: to be troubled; to be in a bind; to have difficulty
meanings.note: Godan verb.

examples.trans: That puts me in a bind.

examples.text: お金がなくて困っている。
examples.trans: I'm in trouble because I have no money.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Directly modifies a noun near the speaker (この店, この辺, この部分).

examples.text: この本は人気があります。

meanings.note: Native counter reading ふたり; shops politely say お二人様 for 'party of two'.

examples.trans: The two of us go together.

examples.text: この二人、姉妹なんですよ。
examples.trans: These two girls are actually sisters.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken counterpart of なぜ or どうして.

examples.text: なんで知っているんですか。

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Temporal noun often used adverbially.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: 最近は小遣い欲しさに身分を偽る未成年も多い。
examples.trans: Lately many minors fake their age using an older sister's ID for pocket money.

examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

examples.text: 最近は小遣い欲しさに身分を偽る未成年も多い。
examples.trans: Lately many minors fake their age using an older sister's ID for pocket money.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

examples.text: 児童福祉法違反だ。お前のビデオに未成年が出てんだよ。
examples.trans: Violation of the Child Welfare Act. A minor appeared in your video.

examples.text: 最近は小遣い欲しさに身分を偽る未成年も多い。
examples.trans: Lately many minors fake their age using an older sister's ID for pocket money.

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: I-adjective; 多くて means 'at most'.

examples.text: 今日は人が多いですね。
examples.trans: There are a lot of people today.

meanings.note: Points to the place where the speaker currently stands.

examples.text: ここに座ってください。

meanings.en: nothing more than (after past verb); up to
meanings.note: After a plain verb + です (出店したまでです), modestly states 'we simply did that and nothing more'.

examples.text: 念のため聞いたまでです。
examples.trans: I merely asked just in case.

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。
お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').

examples.text: ここまでそっくりな免許を持ってこられたら見分けがつきません。
examples.trans: When someone brings a license this identical, even we cannot tell them apart.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Godan verb; 持ってくる means 'bring'.
Attaches to the irrealis (a-stem) of godan verbs.

examples.trans: I was called by the teacher.

meanings.note: Attaches to a past-stem verb form to set up a condition ('if a fire starts').

examples.text: 火事になったら大変です。
examples.trans: If a fire breaks out, it will be terrible.

examples.text: 家に帰ったら電話します。
examples.trans: I will call when I get home.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb: blunt imperative 見ろ ('look!') is rough command speech.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.

examples.text: こちらをポケットにしまっていただければ。
examples.trans: If you could simply tuck this envelope into your pocket.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Auxiliary godan verb following て-form.

examples.text: つい忘れてしまいました。
本を全部読んでしまった。
examples.trans: I finished reading the whole book.

meanings.note: Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Adverb emphasizing that there is nothing more.

examples.text: ただ本当のことを言っただけです。
ただ静かに待っていた。

meanings.note: Conditional particle attached to the hypothetical (e) stem of verbs and adjectives.

examples.text: 練習すれば上手になります。
examples.trans: If you practice, you will get better.
If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

examples.text: うな重を三つ特上でごちそういたしますよ。
examples.trans: Let me treat the three of you to deluxe grilled eel boxes.

examples.text: はいはい、お疲れさま。うな重キャンセル。
examples.trans: All right, good work, gentlemen. Cancel the eel boxes.

meanings.note: Native Japanese counter for three general items.

examples.text: 単語を三つ覚えました。
みかんが三つあります。
うな重を三つ特上でごちそういたしますよ。
examples.trans: Let me treat the three of you to deluxe grilled eel boxes.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Humble (kenjougo) equivalent of する, used in polite business and apologetic expressions.

examples.text: すぐにご連絡いたします。
examples.trans: I will contact you right away.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Between の and な (あなたのような人), describes someone or something 'like ...'.

examples.text: 春のような暖かい日です。
examples.trans: It is a warm day like spring.

examples.text: あなたのような人を探していました。
examples.trans: I was looking for someone like you.

examples.text: 監督、時間です。急ぎましょう。
examples.trans: Director, it is time to go. Let's hurry.

examples.text: いらねえよ！嫌いなんだようなぎはよ。
examples.trans: I don't want it! I hate eel anyway.

examples.text: 金さえ払えば、村西さんは釈放される。
examples.trans: As long as we pay the money, Muranishi will be released.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Calls someone's attention ('look here!') or asks for a brief pause (ちょっと待って).

examples.text: ちょっと待ってください。
ちょっと見てください。

meanings.note: て-form 待って + ください is 'please wait'; causative お待たせして means 'having kept you waiting'.
Combines どう (how) + いう (say); どういうこと means 'what does this mean?'.

examples.trans: What is the meaning of this?

meanings.note: Repeated はい, used to reassure someone or casually acknowledge what they said.

examples.text: はいはい、分かりました。

examples.trans: Yeah, yeah, leave it to me.

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
